markdown_report:
**Select normalized recency weighting for the corrected GRU4Rec.** At 10% research progress, this remains a feasible intervention with unchanged inference, provided the baseline objective and window distribution are verified.

Three insights follow from the supplied evidence. First, recent-item deletion changes sampled training ranks more than oldest-item deletion, motivating a hypothesis without establishing benefit. Second, older-item shuffling also changes ranks, supporting retention of older context. Third, training margins and qualitative feedback establish neither validation accuracy nor an optimal decay; compatibility and ownership remain unobserved.

Three literature insights refine the experiment. RSS [1] removes sampled targets and reconstructs them from the remaining sequence; it provides related motivation, not direct validation of causal loss weighting. RNN analysis [2] separates memory attenuation from target weighting. Sampled-metric analysis [3] requires keeping diagnostic rankings distinct from the pinned benchmark.

These insights organize three directions:

| Direction | Intervention | Evidence boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Supervision | Reweight recent target losses | Window overlap can erase aggregate recency emphasis |
| Credit assignment | Preserve complete causal GRU computation | Coefficient normalization does not preserve gradients |
| Reliability | Preserve reductions; verify predictor parity | Module checks alone omit routing |

Three atomic ideas follow. Scores are originality/potential/difficulty, each 0–10; greater difficulty means more engineering.

| Idea | Scores | Positive and negative assessment |
|---|---|---|
| Normalized exponential loss weights [1] | 3/6/3 | Originality: explicit controlled adaptation, established principle. Potential: cheap transferable ablation, window-dependent effect. Difficulty: simple reducer, exact gradient parity requires care. |
| Uniform-to-recency training schedule [1] | 4/5/4 | Originality: combines curriculum and recency, familiar ingredients. Potential: retains early supervision, adds unsupported schedule choices. Difficulty: one scalar schedule, another budgeted comparison. |
| Lag-stratified gradient alignment [2] | 3/6/5 | Originality: task-specific analysis, established tools. Potential: reveals local conflict, cannot predict generalization. Difficulty: unchanged inference, expensive backward passes. |

For the selected idea, valid targets receive raw weights from 0.25 at the oldest to 1 at the newest, normalized within each row to mean one. Single-target rows retain weight one. Preserve every causal input and sampled negative. Apply weights independently to each baseline loss term, retaining its mask, denominator and coefficient; averaging rows would unintentionally equalize unequal histories [4].

Interpret this as **within-window supervision allocation**. Overlapping windows determine aggregate interaction exposure; uniformly sampled fixed-length windows can give equal total weight to interior targets. Record the actual sampler before claiming global recency emphasis.

Compare alpha=log(4) against alpha=0 with other settings fixed. First verify uniform-control scalar and every parameter gradient using identical batches, negatives and dropout randomness. Compute losses only on valid inputs to avoid masked NaN gradients [5]. Normalization preserves coefficient mass, not gradient norms, clipping frequency or Adam updates [6].

Train one model per category; select solely through unchanged macro validation HR@10. Preserve seeds, routing, diagnostic interfaces, execution limits and predictor checks. Stronger decay may discard useful supervision; repeated validation selection and sampled-candidate shortcuts remain risks. No improvement is established.

References: [1] [RSS](https://arxiv.org/html/2207.02643v2); [2] [RNN training difficulties](https://arxiv.org/abs/1211.5063); [3] [On Sampled Metrics](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/); [4] [Loss reductions](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.modules.loss.BCELoss.html); [5] [Autograd masking](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/notes/autograd); [6] [Adam](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.optim.Adam.html).

idea.description: Apply row-normalized exponential window-relative recency weights to unreduced causal next-item losses in the supplied corrected GRU4Rec. Preserve its backbone, sampler, optimizer, causal inputs and inference scores. Train exactly one independent model per category. Interpret the intervention as within-window supervision allocation rather than guaranteed global recency weighting.
idea.motivation: Recent-history deletion produces larger diagnostic rank changes than oldest-history deletion, while older-order perturbations remain consequential. This motivates testing a gentle redistribution of supervision while retaining all history, but does not establish that existing recency reliance is insufficient. Strong training margins do not demonstrate validation accuracy, and qualitative concerns about compatibility, ownership and useful complements cannot provide unavailable labels. RSS offers related precedent for recency-biased target selection, but its target-removal reconstruction objective differs materially from this causal weighting experiment.
idea.implementation_notes:
Integrate weighting into the supplied corrected baseline rather than replacing its objective, sampler or model. Before implementation, record each loss term, original coefficient, validity mask, denominator, reduction, regularization placement and clipping configuration. Baseline source was not supplied, so these integration details remain unverified. Preserve separately reduced positive and negative terms independently: mean(positive)+mean(negative) differs by a factor of two from averaging their concatenation when counts match. Never assume a negative-validity requirement also applies to a separately supervised positive term.

Use alpha=log(4) for the primary experiment and alpha=0 for its uniform control, with the same setting across all four categories. For m ordered valid targets in a row, define relative age a_j=(m-1-j)/max(m-1,1), raw weight exp(-alpha*a_j), and mean-one weight w_j=m*raw_j/sum(raw). Single-target rows have weight one. For the current combined pairwise-position interface, valid positions require nonzero input, positive and negative only if that matches the baseline. For separate terms with different masks, apply the same rank-based rule independently within each term's valid positions and explicitly record that choice; their temporal coordinates can then differ.

For a baseline global valid-position mean, retain L=sum_i sum_t w_it*loss_it/N, where N is the original total valid-position count. Equivalently, with q_it=raw_it/sum_valid(raw_i), use sum_i(n_i/N)*sum_t q_it*loss_it. Do not replace n_i/N by equal row weights. Mean-one normalization preserves each row's coefficient mass under the declared mean or sum reduction, without equalizing rows of different lengths. If the baseline uses sequence-balanced reduction, separately normalized terms or another denominator, preserve those exact semantics in an explicit adapter. Add unchanged baseline regularization in its original location and with its original coefficient. Skip optimizer updates on batches with no baseline supervision.

Compute the baseline unreduced objective only after selecting valid features and targets. Masking already undefined operations, including log(0) or division by zero, can still leave NaN gradients. Safe normalization denominators are necessary before division. The supplied reducer accepts an already-valid one-dimensional loss vector and therefore cannot repair unsafe upstream computations. Preserve the baseline's actual logit transformations, positive/negative terms and numerical formulation.

At alpha=0, verify the rewritten scalar loss and every trainable parameter gradient against the untouched baseline before clipping or optimizer updates. Use identical parameters, batches, negatives and dropout randomness; restore RNG states or replay identical dropout draws between paths. Cover unequal history lengths, changed left-padding widths, empty and single-target rows, repeated targets and separate positive/negative masks. Check finite values, None-versus-present gradients, and numerical closeness, starting in FP32 at rtol=1e-5 and atol=1e-6; record maximum differences and any justified tolerance change. This comparison must exercise the actual baseline loss path, not two copies of the new reducer. If it fails, fix the adapter before training. These checks have not been executed in this report.

Audit the unchanged family-specific sample_batch window distribution using training-only sampler bookkeeping. Record user selection, endpoint selection, truncation, valid-target counts and overlap exposure. Under window-mean reduction, the expected coefficient of interaction t is A(t)=sum_{W containing t} q(W)*exp(-alpha*a(t,W))/sum_{r in W} exp(-alpha*a(r,W)). For a global-position batch mean, coefficients additionally depend on the batch denominator, so do not apply the window-mean expression indiscriminately. Uniformly sampled fixed-length windows can give equal aggregate coefficients to interior interactions despite within-window recency weighting; boundaries and truncation differ. Mean-one normalization does not correct overlap or restore excluded targets. Persist bounded exposure summaries beneath the trial directory and describe the intervention accordingly. Keep the sampler unchanged in the primary comparison; changing endpoint selection would be a separate hypothesis.

RSS is a distinct algorithm: it samples c=max(1,floor(tau*n)) positions with replacement using p(k) proportional to alpha_RSS^(n-k), removes selected positions while preserving remaining order, and trains a final representation to reconstruct selected items. Duplicate draws collapse, with position inclusion probability 1-(1-p(k))^c. Reported defaults include tau=0.2, alpha_RSS=0.8 and length cap 50. It does not establish the proposed ordinary next-item weighting or a random-window endpoint distribution. The proposed rule retains all targets and causal contexts; its adjacent raw-weight ratio corresponds to alpha_RSS=4^(-1/(m-1)) for m>1. Its window-mean coefficients equal conditional target-sampling probabilities only when sampling leaves inputs unchanged, which RSS does not.

Log valid-target counts and per-row weight ESS=(sum w)^2/sum(w^2), describing ESS as weight concentration rather than independent sample count. Correlated positions invalidate an independent-sample interpretation. Coefficient normalization does not preserve gradient norm, direction, cancellation, clipping frequency, or Adam updates. Record bounded aggregate pre-clipping gradient norms and clipping rates if clipping is present, using the same collection policy in both trials. Optional older-versus-recent gradient alignment should separate recurrent parameters and embeddings, use unweighted losses on the same checkpoint, and remain a budgeted diagnostic rather than a training objective or selection metric.

Retain Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl; DATA_DIR remains os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'] and artifacts stay beneath the current trial directory. Preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, single-GPU execution, 200 batches per epoch and at most 200 epochs. All training, diagnostics, debugging and failures count against the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Do not reuse other-trial checkpoints, average checkpoints, fuse scores or introduce fitted auxiliary predictors. Train the uniform control and weighted proposal independently from the supplied corrected cold start, subject to remaining budget; do not claim a controlled comparison if only one arm is completed. Record runtime, selected epoch, per-category validation results and the macro average for every completed comparison. Preserve the baseline checkpoint-selection procedure and use only allowed validation information through the unchanged host evaluator; no improvement is claimed here.

Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), and all ModelView hooks, with the actual trained nn.Module exposed as view.model. Preserve B x L feature alignment, item_emb, predict_score, user_train, meta_data, review_data and the public loader yield (None, sequence, positive, negative). Retain measured metrics and definitions; unavailable attributes remain unavailable. Diagnostic RNG consumption must not change training draws. Preserve five real training users per category for full-catalog unseen-item simulator recommendations without fitting a second predictor. Anonymous diagnostic prefixes do not support user-bootstrap intervals.

This loss-only intervention requires no architecture or predictor-writer change; retain the corrected writer and verify its actual checkpoint-loaded candidate scores and all four category routes when the host permits. Cover empty and single-item histories and different padding widths, starting at FP32 rtol=1e-5 and atol=1e-6. Read final features at the maximum nonpadding index, never count-1, and retain baseline empty-history behavior and fresh recurrent state per independent history. Do not infer generated-predictor parity from module serialization alone. If actual generated-predictor access is unavailable, report that limitation.

Keep the search small: the primary control and fixed 4:1 proposal precede any schedule or gradient-study extension. Repeated validation selection can overfit 200 users per category. Recent targets may encode changing popularity or exposure rather than more specific interests; weighting can also retain or amplify user-history-length effects already present in the baseline. Describe training-frequency and history-length strata using training-derived definitions, without changing selection metrics or interpreting them as evidence of personalization. RSS, perturbation sensitivity and local gradient conflict do not establish improved next-item accuracy. Do not infer ownership, compatibility, ratings, reviews, simulator traits or causal preferences. No external data, pretrained weights, hidden test files, split changes or evaluator changes are permitted.
idea.pseudocode:
import math
import torch


def recency_weights(valid, alpha=math.log(4.0)):
    """Mean-one weights over each row's ordered valid positions."""
    if valid.ndim != 2 or valid.dtype != torch.bool:
        raise ValueError('valid must be a B x L boolean tensor')
    if not math.isfinite(alpha) or alpha < 0:
        raise ValueError('alpha must be finite and nonnegative')

    count = valid.sum(dim=1, keepdim=True)
    ordinal = valid.long().cumsum(dim=1) - 1
    age = (count - 1 - ordinal).float()
    age = age / (count - 1).clamp_min(1).float()
    age = torch.where(valid, age, torch.zeros_like(age))
    raw = torch.exp(-alpha * age) * valid.float()
    mass = raw.sum(dim=1, keepdim=True)
    weights = raw * count.float() / mass.clamp_min(1e-12)
    ess = mass.square() / raw.square().sum(
        dim=1, keepdim=True).clamp_min(1e-12)
    diagnostics = {
        'valid_positions': int(count.sum().item()),
        'valid_positions_per_row': count.squeeze(1).detach().cpu().tolist(),
        'ess_per_row': ess[count.ne(0)].detach().cpu().tolist(),
        'ess_definition': 'weight concentration; not independent sample count',
    }
    return weights, diagnostics


def reduce_valid_term(valid_losses, valid, alpha=math.log(4.0),
                      reduction='mean', mean_denominator=None):
    """Reduce one baseline term without computing invalid-position losses.

    valid_losses: 1-D losses computed ONLY from features/targets selected
                  by valid, in PyTorch boolean-index traversal order.
    valid: the unchanged baseline B x L validity mask for this term.
    mean_denominator: baseline denominator for a global mean; None means
                      valid.sum(). Other reduction forms need an adapter.
    """
    if reduction not in ('mean', 'sum'):
        raise ValueError('Preserve other baseline reductions explicitly')
    weights, diagnostics = recency_weights(valid, alpha)
    if valid_losses.ndim != 1:
        raise ValueError('Expected a vector of already-valid losses')
    if valid_losses.numel() != diagnostics['valid_positions']:
        raise ValueError('Loss vector does not match the validity mask')
    if valid_losses.numel() == 0:
        return None, diagnostics
    if not bool(torch.isfinite(valid_losses).all()):
        raise FloatingPointError('Nonfinite valid baseline losses')

    total = (weights[valid] * valid_losses.float()).sum()
    if reduction == 'sum':
        if mean_denominator is not None:
            raise ValueError('A sum reduction has no mean denominator')
        return total, diagnostics

    denominator = (valid.sum() if mean_denominator is None
                   else mean_denominator)
    denominator = torch.as_tensor(
        denominator, device=total.device, dtype=total.dtype)
    if denominator.numel() != 1:
        raise ValueError('Expected a scalar baseline denominator')
    if not bool(torch.isfinite(denominator)) or not bool(denominator > 0):
        raise ValueError('Baseline mean denominator must be finite and positive')
    return total / denominator, diagnostics

# Separately reduced positive/negative terms:

originality.positive: The proposal explicitly controls within-window temporal allocation while preserving causal contexts and each baseline term's coefficient mass.
originality.negative: Exponential weighting and recency-biased supervision are established; correcting reductions and exposure interpretation improves rigor rather than algorithmic novelty.

future_potential.positive: A small controlled experiment can clarify whether supervision allocation helps the fixed four-category recurrent benchmark and motivate later exposure-aware studies.
future_potential.negative: Window overlap may neutralize aggregate recency emphasis, existing temporal reliance may already suffice, and gains could reflect popularity or sampled-evaluation alignment.

code_difficulty.positive: The core intervention uses standard tensor operations and preserves architecture, sampling, checkpoint format and inference.
code_difficulty.negative: Faithful integration requires baseline term and denominator inspection, safe valid-input computation, every-parameter gradient parity, and sampler-exposure bookkeeping.

related_work.title: Recency Sampling for Next-Item Recommendation
contributions: Provides related precedent for recency-biased target selection with sequential recommenders, including GRU4Rec.
RSS samples positions with replacement, removes selected positions and trains a final sequence representation to reconstruct the selected items; duplicate draws collapse.
Algorithm 1 and section 5.3 specify the sampling procedure and settings, including tau=0.2, alpha=0.8 and sequence length capped at 50.
limitations: RSS changes contexts and supervision; it is not exponential weighting of ordinary causal next-item losses.
It does not establish a random-window endpoint distribution or validate the proposed normalized 4:1 decay on this benchmark.
Its fixed per-step decay depends on sequence length, whereas the proposed relative-age rule fixes the oldest-to-newest ratio.

related_work.title: On the Difficulty of Training Recurrent Neural Networks
contributions: Explains recurrent gradient attenuation and instability, separating memory propagation from supervision weighting.
Motivates examining gradient behavior rather than assuming coefficient normalization preserves optimization.
limitations: Does not validate recency loss weighting for recommendation or predict validation benefit.
Local gradient alignment and perturbation sensitivity cannot establish that older supervision harms generalization.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled evaluation can produce misleading model comparisons relative to full-catalog evaluation.
limitations: Does not replace the task's mandatory pinned sampled HR@10 selection criterion.
Neither sampled nor full-catalog ranking reveals unobserved preferences or establishes compatibility.

related_work.title: PyTorch BCELoss documentation: reduction semantics
contributions: Documents unreduced, mean and sum loss semantics relevant to preserving baseline coefficients and denominators.
Supports checking separately reduced terms instead of silently replacing them with a concatenated or sequence-balanced average.
limitations: Implementation documentation does not establish recommendation gains.
The supplied GRU4Rec objective must be inspected before selecting an adapter; BCE is not assumed.

related_work.title: PyTorch Autograd mechanics: division by zero and masking
contributions: Explains why masking invalid outputs after undefined operations can still produce NaN gradients.
Supports selecting valid inputs before computing loss operations and verifying finite parameter gradients.
limitations: Safe reduction cannot repair undefined operations already performed upstream.
Numerical correctness does not demonstrate validation improvement.

related_work.title: PyTorch Adam documentation
contributions: Specifies coordinatewise moment updates and epsilon dependence, explaining why preserved coefficient mass does not imply preserved optimizer updates.
limitations: Does not quantify the effect of temporal reweighting on this model or dataset.
The baseline optimizer must remain unchanged in the primary comparison, whether or not it is Adam.

related_work.title: PyTorch clip_grad_norm_ documentation
contributions: Defines clipping through aggregate gradient norms, motivating matched logging of pre-clipping norms and clipping frequency.
limitations: Clipping diagnostics are descriptive and do not establish useful supervision allocation.
Clipping should be preserved only as configured by the supplied baseline, rather than introduced implicitly.
